related_questions.snippet: Myalgia means muscle pain — something we've all felt at one time or another. Sore muscles and body aches are common after exercise and when you have the flu. Myalgia is usually temporary and not serious. But sometimes, it can be a sign of a long-term condition that needs your attention.

text_blocks.snippet: The ICD-10-CM code C34.91 refers to a malignant neoplasm (cancer) of an unspecified part of the right bronchus or lung, according to clinical resources. This code is used when the specific location of the cancer within the right lung or bronchus is not documented. It is a billable code, meaning it can be used for billing and insurance purposes.

ICD-10-CM: This is the International Classification of Diseases, Tenth Revision, Clinical Modification, a system used for classifying diseases and health problems.
Billable code: C34.91 can be used for billing and insurance claims related to the diagnosis.

text_blocks.snippet: The ICD-10-CM code M62.89 is used for "Other specified disorders of muscle". It is a broad category for a variety of muscle conditions that are not specifically classified elsewhere under the "Other disorders of muscle" category (M62).

list.title: Specificity:
list.snippet: While it's a general category, the "specified" part of the code means the condition should be documented with enough detail to differentiate it from other muscle disorders.

list.title: Examples:
list.snippet: This code can be used for muscle sheath hernias, and other unspecified muscle disorders.

list.title: Documentation:
list.snippet: It's crucial to have clear documentation of the specific muscle condition to support the use of this code, as it is used when other more specific codes are not applicable.

list.title: Excludes notes:
list.snippet: Be aware of the "Excludes1" and "Excludes2" notes associated with M62.89. These notes indicate conditions that should not be coded with M62.89 or conditions that may be coded with M62.89 in addition to another code.

text_blocks.snippet: The primary ICD-10 code for general body aches is M79.10, which is for "Myalgia, unspecified site". If the body aches are specifically located in the limbs, M79.609 (Pain in unspecified limb) or a more specific code within M79.6 (e.g., M79.629 for pain in unspecified arm) might be appropriate. If the body aches are chronic, G89.29 (Other chronic pain) or G89.4 (Chronic pain syndrome) could be used. Additionally, R52 (Pain, unspecified) can be used for pain that is not otherwise specified.
